items.text: Comparing s2D/DBT versus DM/DBT rather than DBT versus DM: whether a low-radiation alternative preserves screening performance, with real clinical and one-year outcomes, represents independent value.

The malignant/benign pathological spectrum and changes in DCIS relative to invasive cancer can supplement overall detection rates, providing clues for benefit–harm judgment; descriptive findings are also useful.
Imaging modality may alter density classification rather than biological density, affecting notification, risk assessment, and supplemental screening, which has independent implementation value.

Within-facility before–after comparisons still confound calendar time, reader experience, and population changes; GEE handling of correlation does not itself eliminate confounding, and the seven facilities and their conversion timing require appropriate analysis.

Without a pre-specified non-inferiority margin, equivalence cannot be inferred from non-significance; rare false negatives and limited sensitivity/subtype precision mean that reducing DCIS does not automatically equal reducing overdiagnosis.

Density is a measure potentially affected by imaging modality, and adjusting for it as a main effect can alter estimates; density changes must be distinguished from age/reader standard drift, and historical C-View data have limited extrapolation to the current platform.
